beginner.summary: For system administrators, support engineers, developers and cloud learners who have used a command line but never written PowerShell. Covers installing PowerShell 7 beside Windows PowerShell 5.1, command discovery and help, the object pipeline, formatting and encodings, variables, collections, operators and regular expressions, flow control, files and paths on Windows, Linux and macOS, CSV, JSON and XML, processes and services, scripts, functions, error handling, debugging in Visual Studio Code, REST calls, modules from the PowerShell Gallery, scheduling, and a server inventory tool as the capstone.
prerequisites: Has used a terminal or command prompt to run commands, change directories and read output
Has a Windows 10 or 11, macOS or Linux machine where software can be installed, or a lab VM with administrator or sudo rights
Understands basic computing ideas: files, folders, processes, services and user accounts
outcomes: Install PowerShell 7, run it beside Windows PowerShell 5.1, and say which edition a given script needs
Find commands and read their help, then chain cmdlets so that objects, not text, flow through the pipeline
Write parameterised scripts and functions with error handling that run on Windows, Linux and macOS where the commands exist
Build and schedule a tool that collects system data, exports it as CSV and JSON and reports failures with exit codes

intermediate.summary: For administrators and engineers who write PowerShell scripts and want to build tested, reusable automation. Covers advanced functions with parameter sets and pipeline binding, ShouldProcess and -WhatIf, splatting and argument completers, script modules and manifests, Pester 5, PSScriptAnalyzer, classes and enums, deep error handling including native commands, remoting over WinRM and SSH, parallel execution, Windows administration with CIM, the registry and event logs, Active Directory, the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK, Azure Automation with Az, secrets management, text parsing, REST clients, database access and pipelines in GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines.
prerequisites: Completed the beginner level or can write scripts with parameters, functions, try/catch and CSV/JSON handling
Has PowerShell 7, Visual Studio Code with the PowerShell extension and Git installed, plus a lab with at least one Windows Server or Windows 11 VM and one Linux VM
Has access to a Microsoft 365 developer tenant or Azure free subscription for the identity and cloud labs
outcomes: Design advanced functions and script modules that bind pipeline input, support -WhatIf and have Pester tests and ScriptAnalyzer rules in CI
Run commands on many machines over WinRM and SSH, in parallel, with correct error handling and throttling
Automate Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft 365 and Azure resources with credentials held in a secret store
Deliver a versioned module with tests through a GitHub Actions or Azure Pipelines workflow
